title: Cocktail Guide and Notes
introduction: Welcome to the ultimate cocktail guide. Here you'll find categories of cocktails, how to create your own, and tips on adding to your bar.

sections.subtitle: Cocktail Categories
sections.body: Cocktail categories help organize drinks by their style and is often categorized by their ingredients. Below you can find the main categories and what defines them.

subsections.headline: Sours
subsections.description: Sours are classic cocktails that balance a base spirit with citrus juice and a sweetener, often shaken and served over ice. THe juice is usually lemon or lime, but can also be grapefruit juice (and sometimes orange juice). Examples of sours include: Whiskey sour, Cosmopolitan, Clover Club, Sidecar and The Last Word.

subsections.headline: Highballs and Fizzes
subsections.description: Highballs are mixed drinks consisting of a base spirit and a larger proportion of a non-alcoholic mixer, served over ice in a tall glass. Examples of Highballs include: Whiskey Highball and Pimm's Cup. More complex Highballs have added juice, liqueurs, or other ingredients. A Highball with the addition of lemon juice and sugar is called a Collins (Such as a Tom Collins). A fizz is in the style of a complex Highball but with the ingredients (excluding the mixer) shaken first. Examples include: Gin Fizz and Ramoz Fizz.

subsections.headline: Spirit-Forwards
subsections.description: Spirit-forward cocktails emphasize the base spirit with minimal mixers, often stirred and served neat or on the rocks. They are usually composed of a base spirit, a modifier (vermouth or similar) and bitters or a small amount of syrup or liqueur. Examples include: Martini, Manhattan, Negroni and El Presidente

subsections.headline: Mocktails
subsections.description: Mocktails are non-alcoholic beverages designed to mimic the complexity and flavor of traditional cocktails. If no alcohol is in the ingredients the cocktail belongs to this category.

subsections.headline: Tiki Cocktails
subsections.description: Tiki cocktails are tropical, often rum-based drinks with exotic fruit juices and elaborate garnishes. They usually consists of base spirits (1 spirit or a combination of different spirits), fruit juices and syrups and/or liqueurs, often deployed in various combinations. These cocktails are usually served over crushed ice. Examples inlcude: Zombie, Planter's Punch and Singapore Sling.

subsections.headline: Duos
subsections.description: Duos are simple combinations of two ingredients. This category of cocktails is similar to Spirit-Forwards when looking a Duos but with one key difference in the modifier. Duos consist of a base spirit and modifier (a liqueur or dash of bitters). Examples include: Stinger and Revolver.

subsections.headline: Champagne Cocktails
subsections.description: Champagne cocktails incorporate sparkling wine with other ingredients and as such, cocktails in this category is quite varied. A champagne cocktail can be created by taking a Sour or Spirit-Forward cocktail and adding sparkling wine to it. Examples include: Champagne Cocktail, French 75 and Morning Glory Royale.

subsections.headline: Juleps and Smashes
subsections.description: Juleps and smashes are refreshing cocktails typically featuring muddled herbs, citrus, and a base spirit, served over crushed or cracked ice. Examples include: Mint julep, Whiskey Smash and Gin Basil Smash.

subsections.headline: Dessert Cocktails
subsections.description: Dessert cocktails are sweet cocktails often served as a dessert. These cocktails usually consist of an alcholoic base such as a spirit or liqueur with some sweet ingredients such as cream, chocolate, or syrup. Another category often used as a dessert cocktail is a Trio. To create a trio a cream or cream liqueur is added to a Duos. Examples include: Alexander (and its variations) and White Russian.

subsections.headline: Others
subsections.description: This category includes cocktails that don't fit neatly into the other classifications.

sections.subtitle: The Cocktail List
sections.body: This is the page where you can choose find and search for cocktails. You can choose between categories of cocktails, which spirit the cocktail must include, or just see all the cocktails.

subsections.headline: The Cocktail List
subsections.description: When you have choosen which cocktails you want to see, you will enter the cocktail list page. Here you can see the different cocktails, search for cocktails by name or ingredient(s), or sort between cocktails. To sort - press the 'up and down' arrow in the top left. You will then see different sorting options such as: by name or creator, favorites only, or only the cocktails you can craft with the ingredients in your personal bar.

subsections.headline: Searching
subsections.description: When using the search function, you can search for cocktails by their name, an ingredient or multiple ingredients. When you search for cocktails with multiple ingredients make sure to seperate each ingredient using the comma ','.

subsections.headline: Favorite Cocktails
subsections.description: If you have some cocktails you really like, you can favorite the cocktail. To do this enter the information page for cocktail you want to favorite and press the heart in the top right corner. Now the cocktail will show when sorting by favorites only.

subsections.headline: Removed Cocktails
subsections.description: If there is some cocktails you really do not like you can remove them, such that you cannot see them. Swipe left on the cocktail from the cocktail list to remove them. If you regret, you can find all of your removed cocktails in the 'removed cocktails' page - located at the bottom of the cocktail frontpage. Here you can select between the removed cocktails and undo your action.

subsections.headline: Creating a New Cocktail
subsections.description: If you have permission you can also create new cocktails. On the frontpage and the cocktails list you will see a plus on the top right corner. Press this and you will be directed to a screen where you can create a new cocktail. Fill out some information and press 'save'. If you change your mind, you can just press cancel.

subsections.headline: Editing a Cocktail
subsections.description: If you have permission you can also edit cocktails. Go to the cocktail information screen and you will see an edit button in the top right corner. Press it and you will see an edit screen. Make our changes, press save, or cancel you want.

sections.subtitle: Personal Bar
sections.body: Your personal bar is used to keep track of which cocktail ingredients you own. If you have yet to fill in your bar, you can use the quick add button to quickly choose bar items you have at home.
